newsitem.title: UK: IGC trims 1997 world wheat crop to 578 million tns.
newsitem.headline: IGC trims 1997 world wheat crop to 578 million tns.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday cut its estimate for the 1997 world wheat crop to 578 million tonnes, compared with a previous estimate of 583 million tonnes.
This compares with estimated 1996 production of 580 million.
The main changes included lower crops forecast for the EU and the United States, and increases for China and central and eastern Europe, the IGC said in its monthly Grain Market Report.
The IGC's estimate for 1997-98 world trade remained at 94 million tonnes, up three million on 1996-97.
"Given better domestic harvests, origins other than the five major exporters should feature prominently on the international market in 1997-98," the IGC said.
World consumption in 1997-98 was forecast at 581 million tonnes and world stocks were projected at 95 million tonnes. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
